head_commit.message:
feat(liveness): v1.00.13 W4 — connect/TTFB bound, hard deadlines, heartbeat-aware liveness (#9478)

Every generic blocking phase is bounded by one resolved policy and every
retry-relevant liveness fact is structured (RL-4/RL-8/RL-9, NP-7):

- llm/http-helpers.rkt: provider-sendrecv/ttfb-bounded — connect+TLS+
  status+headers runs under the policy connect/TTFB window; an established-
  but-silent peer raises exn:fail:network:timeout:stream with structured
  phase 'connect/ttfb (never the full request budget); cleanup runs BEFORE
  the worker is killed. make-provider-http-request gains #:connect-timeout.
- all four adapters: streaming sendrecv and eager send paths pass the
  policy connect-ttfb value; the 900 s budget can no longer mask a silent
  connection on any path.
- llm/stream.rkt: per-read waits are capped at
  min(phase-idle, remaining-total-budget) — a blocking read can no longer
  overshoot the total wall-clock deadline by a full phase window (NP-7).
- runtime/auto-retry.rkt: held-request? consults heartbeat metadata — a
  heartbeat-only stream is live-but-no-content, not a zero-liveness dead
  peer (RL-8); total deadline + flood ceiling still bound it.
- tests: test-stream-liveness-classification.rkt promoted green + extended
  into the W4 matrix (connect/TTFB silent-peer bound with elapsed check,
  total-deadline overshoot prevention, cancellation-responsiveness).

Gates: 18 focused suites green (liveness matrix, conformance, bounds,
policy, arch [empty allowlist], stream, heartbeat, auto-retry, adaptive,
telemetry, context, cleanup, http-helpers, 4 adapters, partial-result).
Broad/security/arch gates follow in the wave report.

workflow_runs.display_title: feat(lifecycle): v1.00.13 W3 — headers, cleanup, structured failures (#9473)

head_commit.message:
feat(lifecycle): v1.00.13 W3 — headers, cleanup, structured failures (#9473)

The request boundary owns lifecycle metadata and resources (RL-5/RL-6/RL-7):

- llm/http-helpers.rkt:
  - build-network-failure-context: machine-readable failure context
    (kind/http-status/response-headers/retry-after-ms). Response headers
    are REDACTED to the retry-relevant subset (Retry-After, x-ratelimit-*)
    — authorization/cookie values never reach failure metadata or logs.
  - parse-retry-after-header: delta-seconds AND HTTP-date forms. The date
    parser is timezone-free (civil-calendar conversion — find-seconds is
    locale-dependent) with a deterministic clock seam (#:now-ms thunk);
    past dates clamp to 0.
  - make-provider-http-request now OWNS every response port it opens:
    idempotent single-owner close on success, status-check failure, read
    timeout, request timeout (cleanup passed to the request-timeout
    wrapper), and cancellation (dynamic-wind post-thunk). GC is only a
    safety net. Provider errors raised by status checkers are re-raised
    with the structured context attached (rendering still human-readable).
  - current-provider-http-sendrecv: injectable HTTP boundary for the
    cleanup-contract tests.
  - Duration contracts widened exact-positive-integer? -> positive? to
    match the downstream wrappers and allow sub-second test durations.
- llm/provider-errors.rkt: provider-error-context accessor (alias of the
  inherited q-error context field) — the boundary-named read for retry code.
- runtime/auto-retry.rkt: structured-retry-after-ms reads the structured
  context ONLY; with-auto-retry no longer feeds the exception message to
  parse-retry-after (RL-7: no string-as-protocol). parse-retry-after stays
  exported for compatibility.
- tests: network-failure-context + response-cleanup suites promoted green
  (6 + 6 checks incl. close-once matrix and 429/Retry-After fixture);
  heartbeat-aware held-request? contract split into
  tests/test-stream-liveness-classification.rkt (@not-test until W4 #9478).

Gates: 14 focused suites green (context, cleanup, http-helpers, auto-retry,
adaptive-retry, retry-telemetry, stream, openai, anthropic, azure, gemini,
policy, conformance, partial-result-preservation).

Part of v1.00.13 (#886, wave #9473).

head_commit.message:
feat(adapters): v1.00.13 W2 — mandatory policy consumption across all adapters (#9466)

Adapters consume one resolved request-network-policy; they no longer
author generic timeout semantics (RL-3/RL-9/RL-10):

- llm/stream.rkt: current-request-mechanism-observer seam — stream-sse-events
  records (kind stream initial thinking content total) and
  make-provider-http-request records (kind body-read read-timeout) when the
  observer is set; the cross-adapter conformance harness observes the real
  mechanism boundary. Zero overhead when unset.
- openai-compatible: one policy per request; streaming consumes
  initial/thinking/content/total from policy; eager body-read consumes the
  policy body-read budget (legacy sse-read, e.g. deepseek 600 / kimi 300,
  replaces the flat 120 fallback — recorded parity fix). Local
  (max 600 ...) formula and resolver call removed.
- anthropic (+kimi eager): policy request budget for setup; policy kwargs for
  stream-sse-events; body-read from policy. Completes the v1.00.12 SS-6
  parity deferral: thinking window 60 -> policy value (min request,
  (min (or override 120) 300)); total 600 -> policy total (2x request,
  600 floor) when request > 300.
- azure-openai, gemini: same one-policy wiring for send + stream.
- tests: conformance harness promoted green (all four adapters, fixtures
  F1 deepseek-style request=900 sse-read=600 and F2 request=90); architecture
  test allowlist EMPTY (strict end state); observer parameter registered
  (SERVICE_HANDLE), inventory count 198.

Gates: 18 provider-focused suites, 567 tests green (policy, conformance,
arch, bounds, stream, model-timeouts, openai, anthropic, azure, gemini,
auto-retry, adaptive-retry, heartbeat, retry-telemetry, transport-arch,
differential-fixtures, change-locality, arch-parameters).

head_commit.message:
fix(ci): package-presence guard for cold user-package-store runners

The setup-racket and prepare-racket-environment actions guarded on the
exit status of `raco pkg show --scope user q`, but raco exits 0 and
prints "[none]" when the package is absent. On every cache-miss runner
(main pushes since e3983d4a, fresh PR branches) the cold path therefore
took the relink branch and failed: 'raco pkg update: package not
currently installed / package: q' (INSTALL_RC=1), skipping all required
checks. PR #9452 merged green only because its own branch runs had a
warm, branch-scoped actions/cache entry.

Fix: compare the trimmed pkg-show output against "[none]" (q_installed
helper) at all three guard sites — setup-racket cache-hit guard,
setup-racket cold-path branch, prepare-racket-environment cache-hit
guard.

Verified locally: absent q selects the install branch, present fmt
selects relink; scripts/lint-ci-readiness.rkt 0 errors; ci-package-setup
preflight green (842 modules). README source-lines metric synced (+7,
classify.rkt fixture exclusion).
